inclusion_rule: Recognizers for whispered, murmured or body-conducted speech that obtain the acoustic model from normal (air-microphone, voiced) speech models by retraining, MAP or MLLR-family adaptation or speaker adaptive training, or that train on the target speaking mode from scratch; design compared is the transfer method and the amount of target-mode data. Boundary: conversion systems without a recognizer, enhancement front ends that leave the model unchanged, and reviews are excluded; multiple reports of one experiment count once.

usual_approach.design: start from a normal-speech HMM and re-estimate or adapt it with target-mode data (retraining or iterative MLLR), at the target time (2004-09)
usual_approach.note: dated: 2 of 3 prior unique studies start from normal-speech models (group's 2003 retraining with 2,100 files; Heracleous ASRU 2003 iterative MLLR with 350 utterances); Tatara 2002 trains a whisper model from scratch (4,000 sentences, 80 speakers). [concurrent]: Jou 2004 (MLLR and retraining, throat-microphone whisper), Graciarena 2004 (MLLR), Heracleous Interspeech 2004 and EUSIPCO 2004 (MLLR). All years (155 unique, ledger pattern; full-text design counts, a study can match several): fine-tuning 86, retraining 81, MLLR 36, SAT 17, MAP 10. Itoh et al. ASRU 2001 (whisper, described through Tatara 2002) is not classified: its transfer method is not stated in the citing text. All-years design numbers are full-text mention counts (upper bounds; 're-estimat' also matches ordinary Baum-Welch training).
